places.name: Hukvaldy
places.country: Margraviate of Moravia (Austrian Empire; today Czech Republic)
places.what: Born into a schoolmaster’s family with six surviving siblings, baptised Leo Eugen; a gifted child of limited means.

places.name: St Thomas’s Abbey, Brno
places.country: Margraviate of Moravia (Austrian Empire; today Czech Republic)
places.what: Enrolled as a foundation ward; he sang under Pavel Křížkovský and occasionally played the organ.

places.name: Prague Organ School
places.what: Expelled for criticising Skuherský’s Gregorian mass, then readmitted; he graduated best in his class on 24 July 1875.

places.name: Leipzig Conservatory
places.what: Dissatisfied with his teachers, and denied a place with Saint-Saëns in Paris, he moved on to Vienna.

places.name: Vienna Conservatory
places.what: Studied composition with Franz Krenn; he left in June, disappointed despite Krenn’s complimentary report.

places.name: Brno
places.country: Margraviate of Moravia (Austrian Empire; today Czech Republic)
places.what: Married his pupil Zdenka Schulzová; he founded and directed the organ school from 1881, later the Brno Conservatory.

places.name: Saint Petersburg
places.what: One of two visits to Russia that year; he took his daughter Olga to study Russian.

places.name: Luhačovice spa
places.country: Margraviate of Moravia (Austrian Empire; today Czech Republic)
places.what: After Prague refused Jenůfa, he went to recover; he met Kamila Urválková, whose love story inspired Osud.

places.name: National Theatre, Brno
places.country: Margraviate of Moravia (Austrian Empire; today Czech Republic)
places.what: Premiere of Jenůfa, dedicated to his late daughter Olga; Prague refused it for twelve years.

places.name: National Theatre, Prague
places.what: The revised Jenůfa was a great success in Prague, bringing his first acclaim and access to the world’s opera stages.

places.name: National Theatre, Brno
places.what: First performance of Káťa Kabanová, dedicated to Kamila Stösslová, when he was sixty-seven.

places.name: National Theatre, Brno
places.what: Premiere of The Cunning Little Vixen under František Neumann.

places.name: Prague
places.what: First performance of the Sinfonietta under Václav Talich; it soon won wide critical acclaim.

places.name: Brno
places.what: Premiere of the Glagolitic Mass by the Brno Arts Society under Jaroslav Kvapil; he revised it the next year.

places.name: Štramberk
places.what: Excursion with Kamila Stösslová and her son Otto, on which he caught the chill that became pneumonia.

places.name: Brno Central Cemetery
places.what: Large public funeral with music from the last scene of The Cunning Little Vixen; buried in the Circle of Honour.

places.name: Sanatorium of Dr L. Klein, Ostrava
places.what: Died of pneumonia at seventy-four, with the second string quartet, Intimate Letters, newly composed.

places.name: National Theatre, Brno
places.what: Posthumous premiere of From the House of the Dead, his last opera, two years after his death.
places.work: From the House of the Dead
